title: Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with the zod result wrapper, not the parsed key
description: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result wrapper instead of just the parsed object, so prisma writes `{success:true,data:{...}}` into `Credential.key`, causing parsing to fail on next load and breaking Google Calendar permanently.

title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys collapse to a single literal key; the expiry claim is never enforced
description: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both produce `"[object Object]"`, so the schema has only one dynamic key which overwrites expiry, causing tokens to be treated as permanently expired.

title: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` Response in the sharing branch, but four callers expect an SDK/axios shape
description: Helper returns raw Response when credential sync enabled, but callers expect parsed body properties like `.data`, causing credential sync to fail for googlecalendar, hubspot, zohocrm, zoho-bigin.

title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` where `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `userId`
description: Passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to sync endpoint, causing it to resolve to wrong user and return another account's access token or none.

title: Salesforce refreshes the token on every instantiation, then builds the connection with the stale one
description: Token refreshed unconditionally on every construction without expiry check, but connection built with old token values before refresh completes, making refresh ineffective and adding unnecessary network calls.
